findings.title: D6 protects a state the parser cannot produce, and its fix mislabels every derived-verdict review
findings.description:
D6 (slice lines 158-162) and SC7 (line 292) describe "a PASS parsed with `fallback_used=True` (verdict read, findings not)". The parser sets `fallback_used=True` in only two branches:
- **Derived verdict** (`parsers.py:972-993`): the verdict was UNKNOWN and findings exist, so the verdict was *not* read and findings *were*.
- **Mismatch** (`parsers.py:1023-1025`): verdict is CONCERNS or FAIL with zero findings — never PASS.

So a PASS with `fallback_used=True` is always the derived case, with at least one parsed finding. Today that case renders its findings and no notice, because `if result.findings:` wins (`persistence.py:517`). A synthetic finding prepended to it hides nothing.

D6's remedy is to render the notice "whenever `fallback_used` is set, after any findings". Implemented as written:
- Every derived-verdict artifact gains `## Findings Not Parsed` reading "A verdict of X was parsed, but no findings could be extracted" (`persistence.py:533-539`). Both halves are false for that case.
- The terminal prints "Review degraded: verdict parsed, findings did not." (`cli/commands/review.py:187-191`) under a list of parsed findings.
- No existing test catches it; `test_persistence.py:656-667` checks frontmatter only.

Two related gaps on the same state, which D4/D5 do not address:
- Capping a derived PASS overwrites `verdictSource: derived` with `imposed`, erasing the #97 signal.
- The synthetic finding says "The model's own verdict was PASS" (line 148) for a verdict the model never stated.

Fix: drop D6 and SC7, and state what a capped derived PASS records.

findings.title: D4 treats "telemetry not reported" as "no tool calls", which is wrong for Codex
findings.description:
D4 (line 135) says `tool_calls_made is None` means no tools were offered and counts as zero. `CodexAgent.handle_message` yields one `Message` with no metadata, so `tool_calls_made` is always `None` there. Yet `CodexProvider.capabilities` reports `can_read_files=True` (`codex/provider.py:24-28`), since Codex reads files through its own sandbox.

- Every Codex code review with a truncated diff and a PASS is capped, with a finding asserting "The model made no successful tool calls". Squadron did not measure that.
- This contradicts the design's own rule at line 216: "`None` means 'not reported'… `is None` checks, never `or 0`, for counts". D4's formula is `(tool_calls_made or 0) - (failed_tool_calls or 0)`.
- D11 already gives Codex a "not reported" path for the model; D4 needs the same third state.

Separately, SC4's `tool_calls_made == failed_tool_calls` case may be unreachable on the SDK path. `_failed_tool_calls` increments only when a top-level stream item is itself a `ToolResultBlock` (`sdk/agent.py:178-180`). I could not open the SDK to confirm the stream ever yields one at top level; the design should verify it.

findings.title: The imposed CONCERNS is fed to loops as a finding to fix, and "stops for a human either way" does not hold
findings.description:
- **Loops.** `ReviewAction` passes `result.structured_findings` into `ActionResult.findings` (`pipeline/actions/review.py:414`). `_resolve_prompt_from_prior_review` (`dispatch.py:370-401`) turns them into "Address the following findings…". In an `until: review.pass` code-review loop (`test-loop.yaml`, the `example.yaml` pattern), the implementing agent is told to address "Diff truncated…", which only an operator config change can clear. The review re-imposes each round and the loop runs to `max`. The design names no handling for this.
- **Checkpoints.** Line 137 says a pipeline "stops for a human either way" because of `ON_CONCERNS`. The shipped code-review steps in `implement.yaml:13`, `slice.yaml:41`, `tasks.yaml:34` and `P6.yaml:16` use `on-fail`; an imposed CONCERNS runs straight through. Only `review.yaml` pauses.
- **CLI exit code.** SC4's "exit code … of CONCERNS" is exit 0, the same as PASS (`_exit_on`, `cli/commands/review.py:398-414`).

The cap is still a valid choice under the plan. The stated rationale is wrong, and the loop outcome needs a decision, for example excluding `review-coverage` from the fix prompt.

findings.title: `sq review pr` posts these results as a PR comment, a surface the design never mentions
findings.description:
PR reviews pass `inputs = {"diff": diff}` (`cli/commands/review_pr.py:389`), so Parts A–C all apply. `pr_comment.py:46-64` builds the posted comment from `result.verdict`, `result.structured_findings` and `result.model`. As designed:
- The imposed CONCERNS and the operator-directed text ("Raise review.max_file_size_bytes…") are published on the pull request.
- A truncated-but-read review posts with no mention of truncation.
- The model line shows the answering model with no "(requested …)".

The Data Flow diagram lists three consumers; this is a fourth, and it is outward-facing. State what the comment shows, or exclude it explicitly.

findings.title: D9's equivalence rule is validated by one sample per profile, and omits gemini
findings.description:
The plan (line 443) requires the design to decide what "differs" means for routed variants. D9 decides dated snapshots and defers everything else to walkthrough step 6.
- **Coverage is per profile, the risk is per model.** `data/models.toml` ships about 20 OpenRouter aliases across nine vendors, including `qwen/qwen3.6-plus:free` — the `:free` form the Risk section itself names. One capture will not exercise it.
- **Gemini is missing.** Step 6 lists "sdk, openai, openrouter, local". `profiles.py:61-67` defines `gemini` as an OpenAI-compatible profile with three shipped aliases.
- **The cost of a false positive is understated.** Line 183 calls it "one extra frontmatter key and a WARNING". D10 defines `requestedModel` presence as the gate-readable substitution signal, and `aiModel` becomes the metrology identity.

Capture per shipped alias, or state the residual explicitly.

findings.title: D10's metrology consequence is larger than "identity changes once"
findings.description:
`derive_judge_config_id` reads `aiModel` (`metrology/identity.py:329`), as the design says. What follows is not stated:
- Graduation matching is exact on `judge_config.model` (`graduation.py:42-47`). Records earned under `gpt-5.4` stop matching artifacts stamped with a dated id, and `select_residual_offers` treats them as lapsed with zero offers (`graduation.py:118-123`).
- `sq metrology graduate --model X` filters on `cell.group.judge_config.model == model` (`cli/commands/metrology.py:571`). The operator must now pass the provider's dated id or get "no recommendation cell".
- It recurs at every provider snapshot roll, not once.

The direction is fail-safe (more sampling, not less). It still needs a line in D10 and the CHANGELOG, plus a decision on whether existing graduations are re-keyed.

findings.title: Claims about existing code that do not match
findings.description:
- **"Its two `review_client` call sites"** (line 370). There is one, at `review_client.py:154`.
- **`test_injection_decision.py` as a direct caller** (line 370). It mentions `_inject_file_contents` only in a comment (line 283).
- **"Reset… at the top of `handle_message`, like `_tool_calls_made`"** (line 105). True for the SDK agent (`sdk/agent.py:108-109`). The OpenAI agent has no such attribute; its counts are locals in `_run_agentic_loop` (`openai/agent.py:410-411`). `_stamp_tool_telemetry` receives only the final `turn` (`openai/agent.py:531-538`), so accumulating models across the loop needs new state or a new parameter the Component Structure does not name.
- **`toolsGiven: [Read, Grep, Glob]`** (line 231). The stamped names are the canonical `read_file, list_files, grep` (`code.yaml:57`, `sdk/provider.py:108-111`).
- **Artifact Contract placement.** The example is labelled "tools offered, none used", and `diffTruncated` is placed "after the tool telemetry pair". Walkthrough step 1 uses `--no-tools`, which renders `toolsSuppressedReason` and no pair (`persistence.py:363-369`). Placement there is undefined.

findings.title: "Diff requested but none produced" has no defined `DiffInjection`
findings.description:
D2 says the key is "always written" when a diff was part of the review. `_run_git_diff` returns `None` on a non-zero exit, an `OSError`, or empty output (`review_client.py:515-521`), and the injection is then skipped (`review_client.py:422-424`).
- Recording `None` writes no key, which a gate reads as "no diff, or pre-927".
- Recording `(0, 0)` writes `diffTruncated: false`, which reads as "saw it all".

Both misreport a run where the model saw no diff — the fact Part A exists to record. Define it, for example as a failed review, or as `total_chars=None` rendered `diffTruncated: true`.

findings.title: Any one successful tool call lifts the cap, including when zero diff was injected
findings.description: One `list_files` call keeps a PASS on a truncated diff. That matches the plan (line 442), but the Value claim at line 27 ("saw the whole diff or read files") is stronger than what is checked. For D3's zero-injection case the exemption is weaker still: no read-only tool can reconstruct a diff (`review_client.py:149-153`, issue #81). Reachability is low with defaults (100,000 per file against 500,000 total, `config/keys.py:98-114`).
